---
title: "Part II: the longline fishery"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9,
                      fig.height = 4.5, dev = "ragg_png", dpi = 110)
```

Part II generates set-by-set pelagic longline operations on top of the
biomass truth and keeps the **complete truth of the fishing process**: the
latent strategy, the density at the set, every component of the
catchability, the expected catch and so on. The causal order is

> biomass → fleets → vessels → trips → sets → location → strategy → gear →
> catchability → expected catch → true catch → companion species

Effort is always the number of **hooks** per set. Everything that changes
the catch per hook (fleet, vessel, strategy, HBF, creep, space, residual) is
**catchability**.

```{r setup}
library(pelagicOM)
library(ggplot2)
sim  <- simulate_biomass(om_biomass_config("BET_ICCAT"), verbose = FALSE)
fcfg <- om_fishery_config("BET_ICCAT")
fish <- simulate_fishery(sim, fcfg)
fish
```

Each stochastic module has its own seed (`fcfg$reproducibility$seeds`), so
changing one process does not reshuffle the draws of the others:

```{r}
unlist(fcfg$reproducibility$seeds)
```

## 1. Fleets

Each fleet has:

* a size (vessel slots kept active) and a period of activity;
* access to a set of regions, and a centre with a spread for its baseline
  spatial preference;
* seasonal weights for its trips and an effort trend (median hooks per set);
* an HBF multiplier and a composition of fishing strategies;
* a fleet effect on log q.

```{r}
knitr::kable(fish$fleets)
```

New fleets can be created with [`om_fleet()`](../reference/om_fleet.html).

## 2. Vessels, trips and sets

Each fleet keeps `n_vessels` slots filled. When a vessel retires (career
~ N(`career_mean`, `career_sd`), at least `career_min` years), a new vessel
enters the following year. The first cohort gets a uniform remaining career
so that exits are staggered. Each vessel-year makes 5-10 trips, each in a
quarter drawn with the fleet weights, and each trip makes 8-15 sets
(`sets$unit = "per_trip"`). The alternative `"per_vessel_year"` draws 8-15
sets per vessel-year, which is the literal original specification.

```{r}
head(fish$vessels)
nrow(fish$trips)
```

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
av <- active_vessels_by_year(fish$vessel_years)
av$Year <- as.integer(as.character(av$Year))
ggplot(av, aes(Year, n_vessels, colour = Fleet)) +
    geom_line() + scale_colour_grey(end = 0.75) +
    labs(y = "Active vessels") + theme_pub()
```

```{r, fig.height = 4}
fig_effort_time(fish)
```

## 3. Where the sets are made

Within its footprint, a fleet chooses the cell of a set with probability

$$
P(s) \propto D(y, s)^{\theta}\; g_f(s)
$$

* $\theta$ is `preferential_sampling_strength` (1 in the base; 0 removes the
  dependence on density).
* $g_f$ is a Gaussian preference around the fleet centre.
* The **footprint** is the accessible area (regions of the fleet), revealed
  from the centre outwards as the fleet expands (`expansion_profile`, a
  function of the years since the fleet started).
* With probability `fidelity`, a set repeats the cell of the previous set
  of the same vessel-year.

```{r}
str(fcfg$spatial)
table(fish$data$SpatialChoice) / nrow(fish$data)
```

```{r, fig.height = 8}
fig_effort_maps(fish)
```

## 4. Fishing strategy and gear

The latent strategy (S1, S2, S3) of each set is drawn from the fleet
composition. The odds of `drift_level` (S1) grow in time
(`drift_S1_odds`). Hooks per set are lognormal around the fleet median
(CV `hooks_cv`, truncated to `hooks_range`). HBF follows the median of the
strategy, multiplied by the fleet multiplier, a persistent vessel habit and
lognormal noise per set:

```{r}
str(fcfg$gear$hbf_by_strategy)
```

```{r, fig.height = 3.5, fig.width = 11}
fig_strategy(fish)
```

```{r}
fig_gear(fish)
```

## 5. Catchability

$$
\begin{aligned}
\log q = \log q_0 &+ \beta_{fleet} + b_{vessel} + \beta_{strategy} + f(HBF) \\
&+ c\,(y - y_0) + \beta_{quarter} + \beta_{region} + Z_q(s) + e
\end{aligned}
$$

The terms are:

* $b_{vessel}$ is a persistent random vessel effect (`vessel_sd`);
* $f(HBF)$ is saturating, $a(1 - e^{-b(h-4)})$, centred at the reference
  HBF;
* $c$ is the creep (1% per year in the base);
* $Z_q$ is a persistent spatial field of catchability;
* $e$ is a residual per set.

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
hb <- data.frame(HBF = 4:26)
hb$effect <- hbf_effect_fun(hb$HBF, fcfg$catchability$hbf)
ggplot(hb, aes(HBF, effect)) + geom_line() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = fcfg$catchability$hbf$ref, linetype = "22") +
    labs(y = "f(HBF) in log q") + theme_pub()
```

```{r}
fig_catchability_time(fish)
```

```{r, fig.height = 7}
fig_catchability_factors(fish)
```

```{r, fig.width = 6}
fig_vessel_effects(fish)
```

```{r}
cq <- catchability_summary_table(fish$data)
knitr::kable(head(cq[cq$factor != "Year", c("factor", "level", "n_sets",
                                            "mean_log_q")], 12), digits = 3)
```

## 6. Catch of the target species

The expected catch of a set is $\mu = q \times \text{Hooks} \times D(y, s)$.
Density is used, not biomass, because the gear samples a local volume. The
true catch is drawn from a Tweedie distribution (compound Poisson-Gamma,
power `power`, dispersion `dispersion`) or, optionally, from a
delta-lognormal one:

```{r}
str(fcfg$catch_process)
set.seed(1)
x <- rtweedie_cpg(rep(0.5, 1e5), p = 1.4, phi = 1)
c(mean = mean(x), prop_zero = mean(x == 0))
```

```{r, fig.height = 7}
fig_catch_distribution(fish)
```

## 7. Companion species

Each companion species $j$ has an expected catch

$$
\begin{aligned}
\log \mu_j = \log(\text{ref}_j/1000) &+ \log(\text{Hooks}) + \beta_j[\text{strategy}] + h_j\, g(HBF) \\
&+ E_j(\text{lat}) + \log T_j(y) + e
\end{aligned}
$$

and a Tweedie catch. The composition of the catch is the **signature of the
latent strategy**: deep sets (S1) catch BET and ALB, shallow sets (S3) catch
SWO and BSH. Methods based on clusters or on direct principal components
look for exactly this signature.

```{r}
str(fcfg$species$params$SWO)
```

```{r}
fig_species_composition(fish)
strategy_recovery_diagnostic(fish$data, fcfg)$summary
```

## 8. Nominal CPUE versus the truth

```{r, fig.height = 8}
fig_cpue_vs_biomass(fish)
```

```{r}
fig_cpue_fleet_strategy(fish)
```

The log-log slope of nominal CPUE on true biomass is a quick diagnostic of
hyperstability (β < 1):

```{r}
tg <- cpue_biomass_table(fish$data, fish$truth)
tr <- cpue_biomass_table(fish$data, fish$truth, "Region")
knitr::kable(rbind(cpue_biomass_slopes(tg), cpue_biomass_slopes(tr)),
             digits = 3)
```

## 9. Structural checks

`simulate_fishery()` always runs `check_fishery_truth()`, which stops on any
violation:

* non-negative, finite catches;
* hooks and HBF within their ranges;
* identifier hierarchy (set within trip within vessel within fleet);
* cells and coordinates taken from the biomass truth;
* regional access of each fleet;
* vessel active in the year of the set;
* the identity $E[C] = q \times \text{Hooks} \times D$.

```{r}
check_fishery_truth(fish$data, fish$truth, fish$vessels, fcfg)
```

All twelve figures are available through `fishery_figures(fish, scenarios)`
and `make_fishery_figures()`. The diagnostic tables are listed in
`?fishery_diagnostics`.
